newsitem.title: UK: BP Chemicals loses patent case, may reappeal.
newsitem.headline: BP Chemicals loses patent case, may reappeal.

text.p: British Petroleum's chemicals division lost a patent-related legal case against Hoechst Celanese Corporation of the U.S. in an English court on Friday which could lead to a payment of "tens of millions of pounds", Hoechst Celanese' lawyers said.

The court found BP Chemicals and another firm, Purolite International Ltd, had infringed the Hoechst Celanese patent which covers an invention for removing alkyl iodides from pure acetic acid, said the lawyers in a statement.
Both Hoechst Celanese and BP manufacture large quantities of acetic acid. BP said in a statement it was dissapointed with the court's ruling and it was considering an appeal.
The company also said it would have very little impact on its current manufacturing operations.

"This judgement has minimal impact on BP Chemicals current manufacturing operations, its customers and those other companies which licence an acetic acid process from BP Chemicals," said the statement.
The court did not rule on damages which will be the subject of another proceeding.
When asked a spokeswoman for BP Chemicals said the court judgement would have no effect on the company's plans to install a faster and more efficient acetic acid technology called Cativa.
